conviction.notes: Widened to 53 models across 6 Amazon sweeps + 4 editorial sources; 10 shortlisted onto the curve. Triangulated via CR (lab + reliability survey + measured dB), DehumidifierBuyersGuide (measured dB/IEF), Amazon (live prices + critical-review histograms), and Reddit (multi-year longevity). The wider net confirmed the pick and surfaced a real budget-frontier alternative (Midea 30-pint traditional, $178). Central tradeoff — quiet+efficiency (Midea Cube) vs proven longevity (hOmeLabs) — understood. The 50-pint+pump early-death dealbreaker is isolated to that variant.

title: Basement dehumidifier
subtitle: Small, mildly-damp basement · gravity-hose drain to a floor drain · quiet · ≤ $350 · 53 considered, 10 shortlisted

verdict.headline: Midea Cube 20-Pint (MAD20S1QWT)
verdict.pick_blurb: The knee of the price-vs-performance curve across 53 models: the quietest unit Consumer Reports has ever tested, ENERGY STAR Most Efficient, gravity-hose drain (no pump), and cheap. For a mildly-damp basement, 20-pint is enough — and the small, pumpless Cube is the reliable tier of the family.
verdict.runner_up_blurb: The Reddit reliability champion — owners routinely report 5+ trouble-free years. ~$20 more, louder, less efficient, so it lands just off the frontier. Buy it if a proven multi-year track record matters more to you than quiet.
verdict.headroom_blurb: If the basement turns out damper than "mild," the 35-pint Cube is the same whisper-quiet/efficient platform (CR's highest-rated model), +$30 for capacity margin.
verdict.budget_blurb: Cheapest credible option on the frontier: the Midea 30-pint traditional at ~$178 with 6,900 ratings at 4.4★ — louder and plainer than the Cube, but a proven workhorse if you want to spend the least without dropping to a no-name brand.
verdict.tradeoff: Quiet + efficiency (Midea Cube) vs. proven longevity (hOmeLabs) vs. lowest price (Midea 30 traditional). The pick leans Cube 20 because your stated must ("not too noisy"), the cheaper-is-better steer, and the energy weight all favor it, and the reliability risk is mitigated by going small + pumpless.
verdict.avoid: Any Midea 50-pint WITH built-in pump (confirmed early-death pattern, and you don't need a pump), and the swarm of no-name Amazon brands (AEOCKY, Landeagle, FreAire, VEVOR, Shinco, etc.) — cheap, but 5.0★ on a handful of reviews with no reliability track record (L10).

products.name: Midea Cube 20-Pint

specs.noise: Quietest model in all CR tests (~46-48 dB class)

sources.detail: small Cube 'chugging 2 years'; '20-pinter still going after 2yr' (Amazon)

products.highlights: Quietest, most efficient, cheapest of the credible options, right-sized for a mildly-damp basement. The small pumpless Cube is the reliable tier of the line — an owner of multiple Cubes reports the 20-pint "still going after almost two years" while his 50-pinters died at one year. Set it to ~50% RH, run the hose to your floor drain, and forget it.

products.name: hOmeLabs 35-Pint (4,500 sq ft class)
products.highlights: The crowd's reliability pick. In a 131-comment r/homeowners thread titled "which dehumidifier hasn't died on you yet," the top answers were hOmeLabs: "rock solid for about five years" (42▲), "fantastic unit" (91▲, top comment), "runs all the time, never gave me leaks" (16▲). The cost: louder and less efficient than the Cube, so it lands just off the frontier given your weighting.

products.name: Midea Cube 35-Pint

specs.noise: Whisper-quiet; CR's highest rating score of any model

price.note: newest 2026 SKU has a thin review base

sources.detail: highest rating score of any model

products.highlights: CR's single highest-rated model overall: whisper-quiet, top energy + convenience. Same platform as the pick with more capacity. Dominated by the Cube 20 only because it costs $30 more for the same performance in a mildly-damp space — worth it if you want margin.

products.name: Midea 30-Pint (traditional)
products.highlights: The budget-frontier option: the plain (non-Cube) Midea 30-pint at ~$178 with 6,900 ratings at 4.4★ — a long-proven workhorse. Louder and feature-light vs the Cube, but it's the cheapest credible, brand-name choice and sits on the Pareto frontier below the pick.

products.name: TCL W25D92 25-Pint

sources.detail: quiet small-cap; very good owner satisfaction
older TCL smart models 3.4-3.6★ — reliability watch

products.highlights: CR flags it as one of the quietest small-capacity units with very good owner satisfaction. Tempered slightly because TCL's older smart models sit at 3.4–3.6★ on Amazon — the longer-term reliability read is thinner than the Midea/hOmeLabs track record.

products.name: Danby DDR020BJ2WDB 22-Pint
products.highlights: Quiet (Danby is CR's second-quietest brand by measured dB) and Energy Star, with a clean 4.5★. Pricey for a 22-pint at ~$237 and a thinner review base, so it scores well on quiet but loses on value vs the Midea/hOmeLabs options.

products.name: Amazon Basics 35-Pint
products.highlights: A genuine value contender: cheap, gravity-drain, with a 3,300-review base at 4.2★ (effectively a rebadged mainstream chassis). Plainer and a touch louder than the Cube; fine if you want a big-brand-adjacent unit for under $200, but the Cube 20 beats it on quiet/efficiency for ~$8 more.

products.name: GE 35-Pint

sources.detail: '8 years','10 years','3yr 24/7 no issues' (multiple); one 'died in 2 seasons'

products.highlights: Strong Reddit longevity (multiple owners at 5–10 years), washable filter, gravity drain. Louder (~52 dB) and one cautionary "died in 2 seasons" report keep it mid-pack on your quiet-weighted rubric.

products.name: Frigidaire 35-Pint
products.highlights: A reliable mainstream name and CNN's overall pick at the 50-pint size, but the measured noise (~52.9 dB) is the loudest of the mainstream brands — a poor fit for a quiet-first basement, so it ranks at the back of the shortlist.

products.name: Waykar 34-Pint

sources.detail: 4.4★/21.4K — high volume but Amazon-native brand; 36 dB claim unverified

products.highlights: Cheapest serious option and anchors the low-price end of the frontier, but the "36 dB" claim is a spec-sheet number, it's not clearly Energy Star Most Efficient, and the huge rating base is an Amazon-native brand with manipulation risk. Fine if price is the only thing that matters; the Midea 30 traditional (+$20) is the safer cheap pick.

products.name: Midea 50-Pint WITH built-in pump
products.rejection_reason: early-death dealbreaker CONFIRMED (pump variant) — and a pump is unnecessary for a gravity-drain setup
products.dealbreaker_evidence: Amazon 23% 1-star bimodal; linux4me: 'two 50-pinters failed at ~1yr'; sw21212: 'don't buy the pump one, not Midea quality'; Reddit '3rd Midea 50-pint in 3 years, compressor won't engage'. Pump is the #1 failure point category-wide (CR).

rejected_over_budget.name: AprilAire E050/E070/E080 whole-house
rejected_over_budget.note: Reddit's bulletproof longevity pick (6+ yrs) but ~5x the $350 cap and overkill for a small mildly-damp basement.

rejected_over_budget.name: Honeywell TP-series (right-sized)
rejected_over_budget.note: CR's top quiet + reliable brand, but the available unit is $382 (over the $350 cap); the only cheaper Honeywell is a $76 mini. Hard to find at the right size/price.
